newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse lower on profit-taking.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade marginally lower on Tuesday as market players took profits after an early rise on the blue-chip DAX index, with support coming from a firmer dollar.

The market was buoyed earlier on by a number of strong earnings reports and as dealers said tension over a widely-expected U.S. rate rise had eased, but profit-taking meant the DAX ended at 3,340.33 points, down 7.25 points or 0.22 percent.

Traders also said it appeared that the German market was benefiting from uncertainty caused by France's move towards early elections, with some investors apparently shifting funds out of French stocks into the DAX.
The DAX-30 index of leading German shares edged up 7.58 points to 3,355.16 in early trade, with June DAX futures stronger meanwhile at 3,362.5, 24.5 points ahead.

These positive indicators combined with an upbeat spring report by Germany's six leading economic institutes and meant that the German market was able to avoid losses despite the overnight fall on Wall Street.

"The German market at the moment is not following the Dow as automatically as it often does," said one dealer, adding that investors were increasingly focusing on the early recovery potential of German stocks.
Earnings strength was visible in the first quarter results of software group SAP, which reported a 54 percent jump in pre-tax profits to 181 million on sales of just over one billion marks.
Its preference shares leapt 8.60 marks, some three percent, to 301.50 as the figures beat market expectations of pre-tax profit of just 155 million marks on 920 million of sales.
The share pared gains amid profit-taking to end up 2.10 marks at 295 marks.

Electronics and engineering giant Siemens continued its recent rally ahead of Wednesday's first-half earnings report, up 1.75 marks to 91.75 on one of the day's best volumes, but ended up 1.20 marks at 91.20 marks.
Engineering group Mannesmann also gained after it detailed its 1996 results, rising 13.50 marks to 656.00 initially, but ended softer, up 8.50 marks at 651 marks.
It earlier said group income from ordinary activities rose to 1.01 billion marks from 911 million marks, although net profit declined to 603 million marks from 701 million.

Haircare group Wella rose 14 marks to 969 marks after it reported stronger 1996 profits and said it expected further growth in 1997, but traders noted that turnover in the stock was limited. The share ended the day flat at 955 marks.
